complexity.notes: The dedup-by-list-scan is the bottleneck: a dense input like [-k..k] produces O(n^2) distinct triplets, and each found triplet triggers an O(len(result)) membership scan, giving O(n^4) worst case. Checking membership against ||a set of the triplets found so far|| drops the scan to O(1) average, and a cleaner fix reaching O(n^2) total with no hashing is ||skipping over duplicate values when advancing low, mid, and high so each value-triplet is generated exactly once||. Appending tuples into the result is fine given the any-order contract, though the examples show lists. On the benchmark's distinct values, duplicates essentially never occur, so the scan is nearly free and measured time reflects the O(n^2) sweep.
complexity.summary: Sorts the array, then for each index low runs a two-pointer sweep on the suffix to find pairs summing to -nums[low]; each found triplet is appended only if it is not already in the result list, which is a linear scan of a list that can grow to O(n^2) triplets.
